name: Co-washing
lead: Co-washing, short for conditioner washing, is the practice of cleansing hair with a conditioner or a dedicated cleansing conditioner instead of shampoo.[1][2] It is mainly associated with dry, sensitive, chemically processed or textured and curly hair.[2]

A 2019 dermatology review describes co-washing as cleansing with a conditioner free of silicones, petrolatum and mineral oils, and reports that it is gentle on hair but may lead to buildup from residues under the cuticle scales.[1] Wikipedia notes that cleansing conditioners clean less thoroughly than shampoo and are often alternated with a clarifying shampoo.[2]
infobox: Conditioner or cleansing conditioner in place of shampoo[2]
Dry, sensitive, chemically treated, curly hair[2]

paras: Conventional shampoo uses surfactants to remove oil and dirt, and it can leave hair rougher and more negatively charged, which is why conditioner is usually applied afterward.[2] Co-washing skips the shampoo step. Conditioners contain cationic surfactants, fatty alcohols and other agents that mainly coat the strand, and cleansing conditioners add milder cleansing agents.[2]
Practitioners are described as avoiding insoluble silicones in co-wash products to limit buildup.[2]

A review in Skin Appendage Disorders, titled as weighing the pros and cons of cleansing conditioners, frames shampoo over-cleansing as a cosmetic problem for frizzy hair and presents co-washing as a method that has become popular among people with sensitive hair. It reports gentleness to hair alongside a risk of residue buildup.[1]
Wikipedia reports that cleansing conditioners are generally recommended for dry, sensitive, chemically processed or textured hair and are often alternated with a clarifying shampoo.[2]
Co-washing is discussed in hair-care circles as part of routines for curly and textured hair. The sources reviewed contain little documented discussion specific to looksmaxxing forums.
No studies found. A 2019 narrative review discusses the advantages and drawbacks of cleansing conditioners but is not a trial of appearance outcomes.[1]

card.summary: Washing hair with conditioner instead of shampoo; gentle for dry or curly hair, with buildup the reported trade-off.
card.note: Reviewed only in a narrative review; may leave residue buildup.

quick.overview:
Co-washing means cleansing hair with conditioner rather than shampoo. It is mostly used on dry, sensitive, chemically treated or curly hair.

A 2019 review describes it as gentle but prone to buildup, and sources note it cleans less thoroughly, so it is often alternated with a clarifying shampoo.
quick.mechanism: Cleansing conditioners use milder cleansing agents and conditioning ingredients, so they remove less oil and product than shampoo while coating the hair strand.
quick.risks: The main reported issue is residue buildup under the cuticle. Silicone-free formulations are generally described as preferred for co-washing. No safety concerns beyond ordinary cosmetic irritation are documented in the sources reviewed.
